subject: Tenant audit pull: formats, partial exports & tombstone deletion workflow
messages:
From: Julia Singh <julia.singh@acme-fin.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
Cc: security@acme-fin.com, IT Ops <it-ops@acme-fin.com>
Date: 2028-06-18T09:14:00Z
Subject: Request: tenant-level audit pull + proof of deletion

Hi Rachel,

We need an extract of audit & access logs for tenant_id: acme-prod-11 covering 2027-11-01 through 2028-05-31. This is for an internal compliance review and to build a chain-of-custody record. Key asks:
- Export formats available (CSV/JSON/Parquet/syslog) and recommended for ingestion into our SIEM.
- Ability to do a partial export (range + event types: auth, key-ops, model-inference).
- Time to delivery and expected file sizes (ballpark).
- Proof we can provide that certain records were later deleted (we need tombstone/hard-delete proof for a subset of user_ids).

I attached a scope workbook to this request. Please loop in whoever owns exports and deletion workflow.

Thanks,
Julia
Compliance Manager, Acme Financial
[Attachment: requested_scope.xlsx (XLSX, 45KB)]

From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
To: Julia Singh <julia.singh@acme-fin.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-06-18T11:02:00Z
Subject: Re: Request: tenant-level audit pull + proof of deletion

Hi Julia —

Thanks for the clear scope. Quick answers up front: we support JSONL, Parquet, and syslog streaming for audit/access traces. CSV is available for small slices but not recommended for high-cardinality fields. We can do partial exports filtered by time window and event_type.

A few clarifying questions before we size and schedule:
- Do you need full event payloads (including request/response metadata) or header-level (timestamp, actor, action, resource)?
- How many unique actors or user_ids do you expect in the slice?
- For tombstone proof, are you expecting a signed deletion attestation, a deletion manifest (list of record IDs + deletion timestamps), or both?

I'll ask Neha to provide the export options and the standard deletion/tombstone procedure we follow. If you can confirm the exact event types and whether you want compressed Parquet, we can give an ETA.

Rachel
Head of Customer Security Liaison
Redwood Inference

From: Julia Singh <julia.singh@acme-fin.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
Cc: IT Ops <it-ops@acme-fin.com>, security@acme-fin.com
Date: 2028-06-18T13:20:00Z
Subject: Re: Request: tenant-level audit pull + proof of deletion

Thanks Rachel —

Payload: full event payloads (we ingest into Splunk).
Estimated unique actors: ~1.2k (mix of service principals and user accounts).
Tombstone proof: we need both a deletion manifest (IDs + timestamps) and a signed attestation that records were removed from hot and cold stores. Legal will want the attestation for the audit file.

Also: if the deletion was paused for legal hold, we need the hold verbatim and timestamps.

Can you provide a preferred file delivery channel? S3 presigned link or encrypted transfer?

Julia

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Julia Singh <julia.singh@acme-fin.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-06-19T08:35:00Z
Subject: Re: Request: tenant-level audit pull + proof of deletion

Hi Julia — looping in technical details below and a sample manifest.

Export formats / delivery:
- JSONL (newline-delimited JSON): recommended for Splunk. Can include full payloads. Supports gzip compression.
- Parquet (snappy): recommended for large historical slices and downstream analytics (smaller footprint).
- Syslog stream (RFC 5424): for customers wanting continuous ingestion into SIEM; we can backfill via syslog + checkpoint.
- CSV: supported only for narrow, header-only exports (not recommended here).

Delivery options:
- S3 presigned links (48-72 hour validity) — default and preferred for large slices.
- SFTP with server-side encryption — available for regulated transfers.
- AWS KMS-encrypted tarball drop (if using our Private deployment + customer KMS).

Retention & deletion workflow (tenant-level defaults and our tombstone process):
- Hot retention (active index): 90 days by default.
- Cold retention (tiered object storage): 2 years by default for audit/access traces.
- Long-term archive: optional up to 7 years (requires add-on and advance notice).

Tombstone / deletion proof process:
1) Soft-delete: records marked tombstoned in index; not returned in live queries. Occurs immediately when delete requested.
2) Grace period: 30 days by default (configurable per contract) during which we retain tombstoned content for restore. If legal hold is placed during the grace window, deletion is paused and we record hold metadata.
3) Hard-delete: post-grace, records are purged from hot index and then purged from cold storage in a two-step background job; final erasure from immutable archives (if used) occurs on configured archive TTL.

Proof artifacts we can provide:
- Deletion manifest: list of record IDs + tombstone timestamp + final hard-delete timestamp (if completed).
- Signed attestation: a PGP-signed statement from Redwood with the scope, timestamps, and the account owner who authorized deletion.
- Audit extract manifest: sample we attach here (example_export_manifest.jsonl) showing field layout and checksums.

SLA / ETA: for the window you requested (7 months), estimate 3 business days to stage and generate JSONL/Parquet slices; 5 days if you require PGP signing and encrypted transfer. File-size estimate: roughly 6–10 GB compressed per month for that tenant profile (so ~42–70 GB compressed total) — we'll produce a precise manifest after you confirm event types.

Costs: export egress + packing + signing — we will provide a quote once format/delivery are confirmed.

Next steps:
- Please confirm full payload required (you said yes).
- Confirm whether you want compressed Parquet (recommended) or JSONL gzip.
- Confirm whether you need signed attestation and legal-hold metadata included.

I attached a sample manifest and included the standard deletion attestation template for your legal team to preview.

Neha Kapoor
Sr. Product Engineer, Compliance
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: example_export_manifest.jsonl (JSONL, 120KB)]

From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
To: Julia Singh <julia.singh@acme-fin.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, security@acme-fin.com
Date: 2028-06-21T16:02:00Z
Subject: Re: Request: tenant-level audit pull + proof of deletion

Julia —

Thanks for the fast confirmation. Summary & action items:
- Format: JSONL gzip for immediate Splunk ingestion; we'll also stage Parquet snappy artefacts for analytics.
- Delivery: S3 presigned links + PGP-signed deletion attestation.
- Tombstone proof: we will provide deletion manifest + signed attestation. If any records are under legal hold, they will be flagged and deletion paused; we will include hold timestamps and the hold identifier in the manifest.
- ETA: staging and initial JSONL manifest in 3 business days (target: 2028-06-24). Final signed delivery by 2028-06-26.
- Cost estimate and formal quote will follow in a separate email (Marissa to own).

Please confirm you approve the delivery plan and dates, and whether you want the 30-day grace to be shortened as an exception (we can discuss contract amendment — default remains 30 days).

Rachel

[Attachment: acme_legal_hold_notice.pdf (PDF, 320KB)]
